messages:
incident-bot: [P0] Dedicated pool helixcorp-prod - GPU allocation at 100%, tenant isolation triggered for single tenant 'helixcorp'. Auto-throttle engaged for non-critical jobs. Paging on-call.

amy.sre: paging @oncall-sre, I'm looking at the pool metrics now.

oncall-sre: ACK. joining vc in 2. Starting triage. Any customer impact notes?

jay.platform: helixcorp-prod dedicated pool shows sustained GPU util 99-100% for ~6m, queued tasks ~240, average token latency spiking, some 502s reported to customer. Non-prod tenants already throttled.

lina.solutions: CS says helixcorp reports timeouts on their billing endpoint (high priority). They are single-tenant in this pool — no cross-tenant spillover.

amy.sre: quick metrics snapshot:
```
/infra check-pool helixcorp-prod --short
gpu_util_pct: 99.8
queued_requests: 243
running_jobs: 312
avg_model_latency_ms: 1890
active_tenant_count: 1
last_scale_event: 2026-03-17T10:12:05Z
```

oncall-sre: thanks. Two possible mitigations: (A) transient burst from shared spare (up to +4 GPUs) for 1 hour; (B) force-migrate some of helixcorp lower-priority jobs to a preemptible slot (requires app-level consent); (C) enable immediate autoscale if tenant policy allows > reserved cap. Which is quickest?

jay.platform: burst is fastest if account contract permission exists. Autoscale is blocked — tenant cap=32, current allocation=32. Burst override needs ops-lead approval. We can throttle batch_size and reduce model concurrency as stopgap.

ryan-cs: I just got on a call with HelixCorp. They confirm timeouts and say they cannot accept batch throttling for their billing pipeline — it's latency-sensitive. They're asking for a temporary capacity bump now.

oncall-sre: tagging ops-lead @amy.sre (you have approval ability?)

amy.sre: I have escalation rights for emergency bursts up to 4 GPUs for 60m when customer impact is high and customer agrees to cost. I approve. :thumbsup:

jay.platform: OK, I'll kick off the burst. Command: 
```
/infra pool-burst --pool helixcorp-prod --add-gpus 4 --duration 60m --reason "HelixCorp billing timeouts - approved"
```

incident-bot: action accepted. Burst job queued (id=bust-361234). Estimated attach time ~90s.

maya-support: Note: logging account billing notification to HelixCorp that we are briefly applying emergency capacity; CS to follow up on cost opt-in.

lina.solutions: contacting HelixCorp rep to confirm cost acceptance and ETA.

[~2 minutes later]

incident-bot: BURST_STARTED pool=helixcorp-prod added_gpus=4 duration=60m id=bust-361234 attached_nodes=2

jay.platform: monitoring metrics. Initial effect: queued_requests -> 38, avg_model_latency_ms -> 210ms. Progress looks good.

oncall-sre: keep throttles in place for background jobs. We'll keep high-freq inference pinned to existing workers.

amy.sre: starting 15m cadence checks with alerts: queue>50 -> escalate, gpu_util>95% after 10m -> re-evaluate.

ryan-cs: HelixCorp confirms they see requests completing and latency improving. They've agreed to cost email.

maya-support: filed follow-up S-INC-76543 in tickets, added billing note.

jay.platform: next steps: 1) monitor for 30m, 2) if util falls to <70% we mark resolved and schedule a capacity review with customer, 3) if still high at T+30 escalate to infra for full order of capacity or migrate some workloads.

oncall-sre: ACK. I'll stay on watch for the next 45m then hand to SRE shift at 11:00.

amy.sre: handing incident to overnight oncall at 11:00Z with summary and playbook. Posting runbook link: https://internal.redwood/incident/runbooks/dedicated-burst.md

incident-bot: NOTE: incident state -> mitigation_in_progress. Owner=oncall-sre.

[after monitoring window]

jay.platform: 30m check: gpu_util 62.3%, queued_requests 6, avg_latency 180ms. Gradual drain confirmed.

amy.sre: marking customer impact reduced. We'll keep post-mortem and billing follow-up.

oncall-sre: preparing short blameless postmortem, scheduling dedicated-capacity-review with HelixCorp for next week.

lina.solutions: HelixCorp requested a formal SLA tweak and increased reserved capacity — added to action items.

incident-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED -> mitigation_successful. Closing live paging.

amy.sre: thanks team. Action items: (1) PM/Account to discuss reserved cap change and contract for burst billing; (2) infra to add more granular pre-burst check (auto-suggest policy); (3) SRE to draft postmortem.

jay.platform: noted.

ryan-cs: I'll own the customer billing follow-up.

maya-support: closing ticket when postmortem is linked.

amy.sre: :white_check_mark: will add runbook tweaks.
